core.purpose: Establish the system-wide engineering foundation and clean architecture boundaries.
invariants: Domain rules remain independent from delivery/runtime vendors.
Every authoritative datum has an explicit owner and source of truth.
All production changes are observable, testable, reversible, and evidence-linked.
No adapter or framework may become the canonical business model.
security: Deny by default at trust boundaries.
Secrets never enter source control or logs.
Dependency and supply-chain checks are mandatory.
tests: Unit tests for domain invariants.
Integration tests for infrastructure adapters.
Contract tests for public/internal boundaries.
E2E tests for critical journeys.
Backup/restore and rollback verification.
operations: SLIs/SLOs appropriate to criticality.
Structured logging, metrics, tracing where useful.
Runbooks for failure, rollback, restore, and incident response.
recovery: Authoritative data is backed up and restore-tested.
Changes define rollback or forward-recovery before release.
Recovery minimizes blast radius.

invariants: Server-side authorization remains authoritative.
UI state never becomes the source of truth.
Critical actions expose clear confirmation/recovery states.
Accessibility is native, not retrofit.
security: CSP and browser security headers.
CSRF/XSS/input/output encoding controls.
Secure session/cookie handling.
tests: Critical-journey browser E2E.
Keyboard/focus/accessibility checks.
Error/degraded-state tests.
operations: Frontend error telemetry.
Performance budgets and real-user signals where applicable.
recovery: Backward-compatible deploys or rollback path.
No irreversible client migration without server compatibility.

mobile.purpose: Mobile application surface with device-aware safety.
invariants: Server remains authoritative unless an explicit offline model is selected.
Local data is minimized and encrypted when sensitive.
Device lifecycle and revocation are explicit.
security: Secure platform storage for tokens.
Certificate/network protections appropriate to threat model.
No secrets embedded in application bundles.
tests: Device lifecycle tests.
Upgrade/downgrade compatibility tests.
Accessibility tests.
Offline/sync tests only when offline capability is selected.
operations: Crash/performance telemetry with privacy controls.
App-version compatibility monitoring.
recovery: Remote session/device revocation.
Safe local cache invalidation.
Backward-compatible API rollout.

invariants: Local state is explicit and bounded.
Business truth is not silently forked onto unmanaged clients.
security: Signed release artifacts.
Secure secret/token storage.
Update channel integrity.
tests: Install/update/rollback tests.
Local permission boundary tests.
operations: Crash/update telemetry where permitted.
recovery: Rollback-capable auto-update strategy.
Local data export/recovery if authoritative local state exists.

invariants: Contracts are versioned and compatibility-managed.
Writes are idempotent where retries are possible.
Authorization is enforced on every protected resource.
security: Authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation.
No sensitive internal implementation leakage.
tests: Schema/contract compatibility tests.
AuthN/AuthZ negative tests.
Idempotency/retry tests.
operations: Latency/error/saturation metrics by endpoint class.
Consumer/version visibility.
recovery: Backward-compatible release strategy.
Consumer migration/deprecation path.

invariants: Destructive commands are explicit and fail closed.
Exit codes and output contracts are stable for automation.
security: No secrets in command history/output.
Privilege escalation requires explicit authority.
tests: Command contract and exit-code tests.
Destructive-action dry-run tests.
operations: Auditable invocation for consequential actions.
recovery: Dry-run/preview and rollback/compensation for mutations.

identity.purpose: Identity, authentication, session, and role boundary.
invariants: Identity proof, authentication, authorization, and entitlement are separate concerns.
Sessions and credentials have explicit lifecycle and revocation.
Least privilege is default.

When CAP-2FA is also selected, a second-factor requirement, once enabled for an account, cannot be silently bypassed by any login path; disabling it requires an explicit, auditable action by the account owner or an authorized administrator.
security: Credential hashing/secure federation.
Session fixation/hijack protections.
MFA/SSO controls when selected.

When CAP-2FA is also selected, second-factor secrets/seeds are stored with the same never-logged, never-in-source-control protection this module's own security obligation already requires for credentials generally.
tests: Login/logout/session revocation.
Privilege escalation negatives.
Role boundary tests.
When CAP-2FA is also selected, login is contract-tested for the second-factor-required path, including a rejected/expired code case.
operations: Auth failure/anomaly monitoring without secret leakage.
When CAP-2FA is also selected, repeated second-factor failures are observable as part of this module's existing auth anomaly monitoring.
recovery: Emergency credential/session revocation.
Identity-provider fallback/lockout recovery where relevant.

When CAP-2FA is also selected, a locked-out user's second-factor recovery (backup codes or authorized administrator reset) follows the same emergency credential recovery path this module's own recovery obligation already requires.

invariants: Tenant context is explicit and immutable within a request/transaction.
Cross-tenant access is deny-by-default.
Sharing/collaboration is explicit, scoped, and audited.

When CAP-INDIVIDUAL-ACCOUNT is also selected, a request under an individual account carries no tenant context at all -- 'no tenant' is an explicit, first-class case every tenant-context check must handle, never a synthetic single-member tenant assumed by default.
security: Tenant-scoped authorization on every owned object.
No tenant identifier may be trusted solely from client input.

When CAP-INDIVIDUAL-ACCOUNT is also selected, an individual account's own records are authorized against the account's own identity directly, not against an implicit or synthetic tenant id, so a bug that hardcodes tenant-scoped authorization cannot accidentally leave individual-account data unscoped.
tests: Cross-tenant negative tests.
Tenant-scoped backup/restore tests.
Shared-resource authorization tests when selected.

When CAP-INDIVIDUAL-ACCOUNT is also selected, an individual account's data access is contract-tested to confirm it works with no tenant id present, and that no tenant-scoped query accidentally matches it via a null-tenant wildcard.
operations: Tenant dimension in audit/observability without leaking sensitive data.

When CAP-INDIVIDUAL-ACCOUNT is also selected, the mix of individual (no-org) vs org-scoped accounts is observable, since capacity/scaling assumptions built around 'one tenant per customer' do not hold once individual accounts are also present.
recovery: Tenant-scoped recovery minimizes other-tenant impact.
Cross-tenant repair requires elevated authority and audit.
When CAP-INDIVIDUAL-ACCOUNT is also selected, an individual account's backup/restore path does not depend on any tenant record existing to restore alongside it.

invariants: Every aggregate/entity has explicit ownership and lifecycle.
Business invariants are enforced close to domain truth.
Vendor/framework semantics do not leak into the domain.
When CAP-INVENTORY is also selected, a stock balance only changes via an appended, immutable movement record; it is never changed by a direct overwrite of the balance figure itself.

When CAP-INVENTORY and CAP-ORDERS are both also selected, quantity committed to an order is tracked as a reservation separate from available quantity; cancelling or expiring that order releases the reservation back to available quantity rather than leaving it stranded.

When CAP-CYCLE-COUNT is also selected, a physical count's discrepancy against the recorded balance is always recorded as an explicit, attributable adjustment movement -- who counted, when, and the before/after quantity -- never a silent overwrite of the balance; this is the same immutable-movement-ledger invariant CAP-INVENTORY itself requires for every other balance change, applied whether the merchant tracks one stock record or, when CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is also selected, counts each location's balance separately.

When CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES is also selected, a product's attribute values are validated against centrally defined attribute definitions and category/taxonomy mappings, never stored as free-text fields that bypass that governance.
security: Sensitive domain attributes are classified and access-scoped.
When CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES is also selected, attribute-definition and taxonomy-mapping edits are restricted to a governance role distinct from general product-catalog edit access.
tests: Invariant/state-transition tests.
Property tests for critical calculations where useful.

When CAP-CYCLE-COUNT is also selected, the discrepancy-as-adjustment-movement invariant is contract-tested: a count that differs from the recorded balance produces an attributable adjustment record, never a direct balance overwrite.
When CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES is also selected, attribute-validation and category-mapping rejection paths are contract-tested for values outside their governed definition.
operations: Business-event/audit signals for consequential transitions.
When CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES is also selected, products missing required attributes for their assigned category are observable as a data-quality signal.
recovery: State corrections preserve audit/history.
Migrations protect semantic meaning, not only columns.

When CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES is also selected, attribute-definition and taxonomy-mapping changes are versioned so existing product data can be re-validated against a prior definition if a mapping change proves incorrect.

workflow.purpose: Workflow, approval, task, and state-transition orchestration.
invariants: State transitions are explicit and validated.
Approval identity/time/reason are auditable.
Duplicate delivery cannot cause duplicate business effects.

When CAP-WORKFLOW-RETRY is also selected, retrying a failed step never re-executes an already-completed step in the same run or duplicates that step's side effects, the same duplicate-delivery invariant this module already requires generally.

When CAP-POLICY-ENGINE is also selected, a policy definition's version is recorded against every consequential decision it produced, so which policy version produced a given workflow outcome is always reconstructable.
When CAP-CHECKLIST is also selected, a parent task configured to require full checklist completion cannot be marked complete while any sub-item remains unchecked.

When CAP-EXPERIMENT-METRICS is also selected, an experiment's reported result is always computed from the same variant-assignment records CAP-FEATURE-FLAGS produced for that experiment, never a separately-tracked, potentially-diverging assignment log.
security: Authorization is checked per transition, not only per screen.
High-impact approvals enforce required authority/dual control.
When CAP-WORKFLOW-RETRY is also selected, manually forcing a resume/retry from a failed step requires the same transition-authorization check as any other state transition in this module.
When CAP-POLICY-ENGINE is also selected, authoring or editing a policy definition requires a separate, higher authority than merely triggering the workflow that consumes it.
When CAP-CHECKLIST is also selected, checking off a sub-item follows the same assignment/authorization scope as the parent task.
When CAP-EXPERIMENT-METRICS is also selected, experiment result data is only visible to staff holding experiment-review authority, distinct from ordinary feature-flag toggle access.
tests: Valid/invalid transition matrix.
Concurrent transition/idempotency tests.
Approval revocation/cancellation paths.
When CAP-WORKFLOW-RETRY is also selected, retry-without-duplication is contract-tested: retrying a step with an external side effect must not repeat that side effect.
When CAP-POLICY-ENGINE is also selected, policy evaluation is contract-tested against a boundary-condition fixture (e.g. a threshold exactly at its limit).
When CAP-CHECKLIST is also selected, the require-full-completion invariant is contract-tested: marking the parent task complete with an unchecked sub-item is rejected.

When CAP-EXPERIMENT-METRICS is also selected, statistical-significance calculation is contract-tested against a known-input/known-output fixture (a case that should, and a case that should not, reach significance).
operations: Stuck/failed workflow visibility.
Transition latency and failure signals.
When CAP-WORKFLOW-RETRY is also selected, retry counts and exhausted-retry failures are observable alongside this module's existing stuck/failed workflow visibility.
When CAP-POLICY-ENGINE is also selected, policy evaluation failures/exceptions are observable.
When CAP-CHECKLIST is also selected, tasks with stalled/incomplete checklists past an expected timeframe are observable.
When CAP-EXPERIMENT-METRICS is also selected, running experiments approaching or past their planned sample-size/duration are observable.
recovery: Compensating transitions or explicit irreversible boundary.
Resume/retry semantics are deterministic.
When CAP-WORKFLOW-RETRY is also selected, a workflow that exhausts its retry limit surfaces as a failure requiring explicit resolution, never silently abandoned.
When CAP-POLICY-ENGINE is also selected, policy definitions are versioned and included in backup scope, so a bad policy change can be rolled back without a code deploy.
When CAP-CHECKLIST is also selected, checklist sub-item state and history are included in backup scope alongside the parent task.
When CAP-EXPERIMENT-METRICS is also selected, experiment configuration and result history are included in backup scope.

invariants: Object metadata and ownership are explicit.
Storage objects are never authorized by opaque URL possession alone.
Integrity/lifecycle are managed.
security: Type/size validation.
Malware/content scanning when untrusted uploads exist.
Signed/short-lived access as appropriate.
tests: Unauthorized object access negatives.
Upload corruption/interruption tests.
Version/lifecycle tests when selected.
operations: Storage growth, scan failures, orphan detection.
recovery: Object/version recovery and metadata consistency checks.

invariants: Search index is derived unless explicitly justified otherwise.
Index can be rebuilt from authoritative sources.
Authorization filtering cannot be bypassed by search.

When CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE is also selected, autocomplete suggestions are derived from the same index CAP-SEARCH itself queries against; they never diverge into a second, separately-maintained suggestion source that can fall out of sync with actual search results.
security: Search results obey the same object authorization model.

When CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE is also selected, autocomplete suggestions obey the same object-authorization filtering this module's own security obligation already requires for full search results -- a suggestion never leaks the existence of an object the requesting user could not otherwise see.
tests: Rebuild consistency.
Unauthorized-result exclusion.
Index lag behavior.
When CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE is also selected, authorization filtering on suggestions is contract-tested the same way this module's own unauthorized-result-exclusion test already covers full search results.
operations: Index lag, failure, size, query latency.
When CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE is also selected, autocomplete query latency is observable alongside this module's existing index/query latency signals.
recovery: Deterministic rebuild/reindex procedure.

When CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE is also selected, autocomplete suggestions are rebuilt by the same deterministic reindex procedure this module's own recovery obligation already requires, never a separate rebuild path.

analytics.purpose: Reporting, analytics, dashboard, and export capability.
invariants: Metric definitions are versioned and reproducible.
Analytics is not an accidental source of transactional truth.
Exports respect authorization and data minimization.

When CAP-METRIC-GOVERNANCE is also selected, a registered metric's calculation is versioned and every consumer resolves the same registered version; a report never silently recomputes its own diverging definition of a metric that is already centrally registered -- the same metric-definition-versioning invariant this module already requires generally, made concrete for named business metrics.
security: Row/tenant access controls.
Sensitive exports are auditable.
When CAP-METRIC-GOVERNANCE is also selected, editing a registered metric's definition requires the same authority as other analytics configuration, distinct from merely consuming it in a report.
tests: Metric reconciliation.
Authorization on reports/exports.
Time-zone/currency correctness where applicable.

When CAP-METRIC-GOVERNANCE is also selected, metric resolution is contract-tested across two different consumers (e.g. a dashboard and an export) to confirm both resolve the identical registered definition.
operations: Pipeline freshness and reconciliation signals.
When CAP-METRIC-GOVERNANCE is also selected, a metric definition change's rollout to all consumers is observable.
recovery: Rebuild derived aggregates from source data.

When CAP-METRIC-GOVERNANCE is also selected, metric definitions are versioned and included in backup scope, so a bad definition change can be rolled back without recomputing historical reports from scratch.

commercial.purpose: Commercial editions, subscriptions, entitlements, trials, and licensing.
invariants: Entitlement is separate from payment-provider state.
Commercial state transitions are explicit and auditable.
Product capability gates are centrally defined.

When CAP-CONNECTOR-QUOTA is also selected, a per-connector quota is checked and enforced as its own entitlement dimension, independent of the account's other usage-metering dimensions; exceeding one connector's quota never silently borrows headroom from another.

When CAP-PREPAID-CREDITS is also selected, a credit balance only changes via an appended, immutable ledger entry (purchase, usage debit, refund, or expiry) -- never a direct overwrite of the stored balance figure -- and a usage event that would take the balance negative is rejected unless an explicit, reviewed overdraft policy allows it.
security: Entitlement checks are server-side authoritative.
Administrative overrides require audit/authority.
When CAP-CONNECTOR-QUOTA is also selected, per-connector quota enforcement is server-side authoritative, the same as this module's own entitlement-check obligation already requires generally.

When CAP-PREPAID-CREDITS is also selected, crediting or adjusting a balance outside the normal purchase/usage-debit path requires the same administrative-override audit/authority this module's own security obligation already requires generally.
tests: Edition/entitlement matrix.
Subscription lifecycle.
Trial expiry/grace period.
When CAP-CONNECTOR-QUOTA is also selected, per-connector quota enforcement is contract-tested at and just above the connector's own limit, independent of other usage-metering dimensions.
When CAP-PREPAID-CREDITS is also selected, concurrent usage-debit contract tests confirm two simultaneous debits against the same balance can never together take it negative (no lost-update race).
operations: Entitlement mismatch and lifecycle failure monitoring.
When CAP-CONNECTOR-QUOTA is also selected, accounts approaching a per-connector quota limit are observable for upsell/upgrade follow-up.

When CAP-PREPAID-CREDITS is also selected, accounts whose balance has run low or hit zero are observable for a top-up/replenishment follow-up, alongside this module's own entitlement-mismatch monitoring.
recovery: Provider outage does not silently corrupt entitlement truth.
Manual correction is audited and reversible.
When CAP-CONNECTOR-QUOTA is also selected, per-connector quota configuration is included in backup scope.

When CAP-PREPAID-CREDITS is also selected, the credit ledger is included in backup scope, and a corrupted or lost balance is reconstructable by replaying the ledger rather than trusting only the last snapshot figure.

invariants: Provider adapter isolates external payment semantics.
Every money-moving write is idempotent.
Ledger/reconciliation distinguishes requested, provider, and settled state.
security: Do not store raw payment credentials when a provider can tokenize.
Webhook authenticity and replay defenses.
tests: Duplicate callback/idempotency.
Partial failure/reconciliation.
Refund/partial-refund state transitions.
operations: Payment failure/reconciliation alerts.
Provider latency/outage visibility.
recovery: Compensation/refund paths.
Provider replay/reconciliation before manual mutation.

invariants: Notification request and delivery state are separate.
Retry cannot duplicate consequential external effects.
User/channel preferences are explicit where required.
security: Template/output escaping.
Secrets and sensitive payload minimization.
Webhook signatures when emitting webhooks.
tests: Retry/deduplication.
Provider failure/fallback.
Template rendering.
operations: Delivery rate, bounce/failure, provider health.
recovery: Dead-letter/retry policy.
Provider switch through adapter boundary.

invariants: External semantics terminate at adapters.
Timeout/retry/circuit-breaker behavior is explicit.
Compatibility and version ownership are known.
security: Scoped credentials.
Inbound authenticity validation.
Outbound data minimization.
tests: Contract tests against provider fixtures/sandboxes.
Timeout/retry/idempotency.
Schema/version changes.
operations: Per-provider health, latency, error, quota signals.
recovery: Fallback/degraded mode when justified.
Replay/reconciliation for missed external events.

invariants: Local authoritative scope is explicitly defined.
Conflict resolution is deterministic.
Sync operations are idempotent and tenant-safe.
security: Sensitive local data encrypted.
Device/session revocation semantics.
No cross-user local cache leakage.
tests: Conflict matrix.
Interrupted sync/retry.
Clock/order skew.
Revoked-device behavior.
operations: Sync backlog/conflict/error visibility.
recovery: Local reset/resync procedure.
Server reconciliation remains auditable.

globalization.purpose: Localization, timezone, currency, and RTL capability.
invariants: Canonical data representation is locale-independent.
Presentation formatting is locale-aware.
Timezone meaning is explicit for scheduled/business events.
security: Localization does not bypass validation/encoding.
tests: Unicode/RTL.
Timezone/DST boundaries.
Currency/number/date formats.
operations: Locale-specific rendering/error telemetry where useful.
recovery: Data remains canonical when locale settings change.

invariants: AI output is not treated as verified fact without evidence.
Model/provider/version and input evidence are reproducible for consequential outputs.
Tool/action authority is explicit and risk-derived.

When CAP-AGENTIC-COMMERCE is also selected, an external agent's checkout intent is honored only if its purchase mandate (spending limit, product scope, expiry) is verified as unexpired and unexceeded before order creation, never after.

When CAP-AI-PROMPT-REGISTRY is also selected, a consequential AI output's prompt version is retrievable from the registry, satisfying this module's own reproducibility invariant for prompt/version evidence.

When CAP-AI-OUTPUT-EVAL is also selected, an evaluation score is computed from the same golden/adversarial prompt sets this module's own testing obligation already requires, never a separate, undocumented rubric.

When CAP-AI-CITATION is also selected, a surfaced citation always resolves to a real, currently-accessible source document/passage; a citation to a deleted or inaccessible source is never silently shown as if still valid.
security: Prompt/context injection defenses.
Data minimization and provider policy.
Tool permission boundary and secret isolation.
When CAP-AGENTIC-COMMERCE is also selected, mandate scope (spending limit, product scope, expiry) is checked server-side on every checkout intent, never trusted from agent-supplied claims alone.
When CAP-AI-PROMPT-REGISTRY is also selected, editing a registered prompt requires the same tool/action authority boundary as other AI configuration changes.

When CAP-AI-OUTPUT-EVAL is also selected, evaluation results feeding an automated model/prompt rollback decision are themselves logged and reviewable, not a silent automatic action with no audit trail.

When CAP-AI-CITATION is also selected, a citation never surfaces a source document/passage the requesting user is not themselves authorized to view, even if the underlying AI-search index includes it.
tests: Golden/adversarial prompts.
Authority/tool negatives.
Model/provider fallback.
Counterfactual tests for consequential decisions.
When CAP-AGENTIC-COMMERCE is also selected, mandate-boundary tests cover an agent attempting to exceed spending limit, buy outside product scope, or act after mandate expiry -- each rejected.

When CAP-AI-PROMPT-REGISTRY is also selected, prompt version resolution is contract-tested to confirm a call site always resolves the registry's current (or explicitly pinned) version, never a stale cached copy.
When CAP-AI-OUTPUT-EVAL is also selected, a deliberately-degraded model/prompt fixture is contract-tested to confirm the evaluation score actually drops and is detected.
When CAP-AI-CITATION is also selected, citation-authorization filtering is contract-tested: an answer drawing on a source the user cannot access must not cite it.
operations: Quality, cost, latency, refusal/failure, provider/model version signals.
When CAP-AGENTIC-COMMERCE is also selected, agent-initiated orders are distinguishable from human-initiated orders in audit/observability signals.
When CAP-AI-PROMPT-REGISTRY is also selected, prompt version usage and rollout are observable alongside this module's existing quality/cost/latency signals.
When CAP-AI-OUTPUT-EVAL is also selected, evaluation score trend over time is observable alongside this module's existing quality/cost/latency signals.
When CAP-AI-CITATION is also selected, answers with zero resolvable citations are observable as a quality signal.
recovery: Disable/fallback/rollback model or prompt version.
Compensate/revert AI actions where reversible.
When CAP-AGENTIC-COMMERCE is also selected, a customer can revoke an agent's mandate at any time, immediately blocking further checkout intents under it.
When CAP-AI-PROMPT-REGISTRY is also selected, prompt version history is included in backup scope and can be rolled back independently of the model/provider rollback this module already requires.

When CAP-AI-OUTPUT-EVAL is also selected, a sustained evaluation-score regression triggers the same disable/fallback/rollback path this module's own recovery obligation already requires for model or prompt version issues.
When CAP-AI-CITATION is also selected, citation-to-source linkage is rebuildable from the same source index CAP-AI-SEARCH itself is rebuilt from.

Rollback rehearsal.

Public and authenticated content paths are separated.
Embedded/public capabilities never inherit internal privileges.
security: Rate limiting/abuse controls.
Session/access controls.
Content security/accessibility.
tests: Anonymous/authenticated boundary tests.
Partner/customer isolation.
Abuse/rate-limit paths.
operations: External journey availability and abuse signals.
recovery: Safe session revocation and backward-compatible frontend rollout.

invariants: Obligations are evidence-backed and freshness-bounded.
Data minimization, purpose, retention, and access are explicit.
Compliance claims never exceed evidence.
security: Sensitive data has stronger access/audit controls as required.
tests: Control evidence tests.
Retention/deletion/export checks.
Policy freshness checks.
operations: Control failures and stale-evidence alerts.
recovery: Breach/incident procedures.
Policy change migration path.

reliability.purpose: High-impact reliability, availability, realtime, and assurance.
invariants: SLIs/SLOs reflect user/business outcomes.
Failure domains and blast radius are explicit.
High-impact changes require independent assurance.
security: Emergency access is controlled and audited.

DR/restore rehearsal.
Human oversight tests for high-impact operations.

invariants: Every custom requirement is preserved verbatim with a stable ID.
Custom text never silently activates an implementation technology.
Architecture review must map each custom requirement to existing or newly approved capabilities before implementation.

tests: Traceability test from custom requirement ID to final mapped capability/module.
