content.purpose: Produce, version, and govern brand/marketing content assets (graphics, video) distinct from general user-uploaded files.
invariants: A published brand asset has a traceable approval record before external use.
Asset versioning preserves prior approved versions, not just the latest.
Digital asset management does not become a second source of truth for files already owned by the files module.
When CAP-CAPTIONING is also selected, a generated caption/subtitle track is versioned alongside the video asset it was generated from, never silently regenerated over a prior human-corrected version.
security: Asset access/download follows the same authorization model as other stored files.
When CAP-CAPTIONING is also selected, caption/subtitle files follow the same access/download authorization as the video asset they belong to.
tests: Approval-workflow gating is contract-tested (unapproved assets cannot be marked published).
When CAP-CAPTIONING is also selected, caption timing alignment is contract-tested against a known-duration source clip.
operations: Content production throughput and pending-approval backlog are observable.
When CAP-CAPTIONING is also selected, caption generation failures/low-confidence transcriptions are observable for human review.
recovery: Approved asset history is included in backup scope.
When CAP-CAPTIONING is also selected, a human-corrected caption/subtitle track is included in backup scope and never overwritten by a later automatic regeneration without an explicit re-run request.

customer_service.purpose: Provide ticketing, live support, and self-service channels for resolving customer issues with tracked SLAs.
invariants: Every support interaction is attributable to a ticket or logged conversation.
SLA clocks pause/resume deterministically on defined status transitions.
Customer satisfaction data is linked to the resolved ticket it measures.

When CAP-OMNICHANNEL-MESSAGING is also selected, conversations from every connected external platform (LINE, WhatsApp Business, Telegram, Instagram/Messenger) resolve into the same unified inbox record, never a per-platform parallel inbox.

When CAP-CANNED-REPLY is also selected, a canned-reply template's content can only be edited by staff holding support-content authority, and every use of one is attributable to the sending agent the same as a manually-typed reply.

When CAP-DOC-TEMPLATES is also selected, a generated document's variable substitution is derived from real, current record data at generation time, never a stale cached copy silently reused across generations.
security: Support agents access only the customer data scoped to their assigned tickets/tenant.
Call/chat transcripts follow the same data-residency rules as other customer data.
When CAP-OMNICHANNEL-MESSAGING is also selected, external-platform message content and customer identifiers follow the same access-scoping as other customer data, regardless of source platform.
When CAP-CANNED-REPLY is also selected, canned-reply templates are stored and access-scoped the same as other support content, never exposed to customers as an editable object.

When CAP-DOC-TEMPLATES is also selected, editing a document template requires the same support-content authority as editing a knowledge-base article, distinct from merely triggering a generation from an existing template.
tests: SLA breach detection is tested against clock-pause edge cases.
Ticket assignment/escalation paths are contract-tested.

When CAP-OMNICHANNEL-MESSAGING is also selected, cross-platform inbox unification is contract-tested: messages from two different connected platforms for the same customer land in one conversation thread, not two.
When CAP-CANNED-REPLY is also selected, sending a canned reply is contract-tested to confirm it produces the same attributable conversation/ticket entry as a manually-typed reply.

When CAP-DOC-TEMPLATES is also selected, template variable substitution is contract-tested against a record with a missing/null field to confirm it fails visibly rather than generating a document with a silently blank value.
operations: SLA compliance rate and ticket backlog are observable.
Escalation paths have a defined on-call linkage.
When CAP-OMNICHANNEL-MESSAGING is also selected, per-platform connector health (delivery failure, webhook lag) is observable independent of overall ticket/SLA metrics.
When CAP-CANNED-REPLY is also selected, canned-reply usage frequency is observable to identify which templates need updating.
When CAP-DOC-TEMPLATES is also selected, document generation failures are observable and alertable.
recovery: An abandoned live-chat session preserves the transcript up to disconnect.
Ticket data is included in backup scope.
When CAP-OMNICHANNEL-MESSAGING is also selected, a disconnected external-platform connector does not lose in-flight message history; reconnection resumes into the same conversation thread.
When CAP-CANNED-REPLY is also selected, canned-reply templates are included in backup scope.
When CAP-DOC-TEMPLATES is also selected, document templates and their version history are included in backup scope.

hr.purpose: Manage employee records, recruitment, attendance, performance, and payroll as an internal operations function.
invariants: Payroll calculations are reproducible from stored attendance/compensation inputs at a stated point in time.
An employee record's sensitive fields (compensation, performance review content) follow least-privilege access distinct from general staff directory visibility.
Attendance/leave state changes are auditable with actor and timestamp.
security: HR data is among the most sensitive personal data categories in the system and follows the strictest access controls.
Payroll processing is not triggerable by any role other than explicitly authorized HR/finance staff.
tests: Payroll calculation is tested against golden known-input/known-output fixtures.
Access-control tests confirm non-HR staff cannot read compensation data.
operations: Payroll run success/failure is observable and alerted.
recovery: Payroll and attendance history is included in backup scope with restore verification given its regulatory sensitivity.

marketing.purpose: Plan, execute, and measure marketing campaigns and lead generation without becoming the system of record for finalized customer/commercial data.
invariants: Marketing leads are distinct from qualified sales opportunities until explicitly converted.
Unsubscribe/consent state is authoritative and checked before every send.
Campaign attribution data is reproducible from stored event history.
security: Marketing sends respect consent/opt-out state from customer data ownership records.
Recipient lists are not exportable outside authorized roles.
tests: Unsubscribe suppression is enforced in send tests.
Segmentation queries are covered by contract tests.
operations: Campaign send volume and bounce/complaint rates are observable.
Automation sequences have a kill switch.
recovery: A paused/failed automation sequence resumes without duplicate sends.
Campaign data is included in backup scope.

procurement.purpose: Manage purchase requisition approval, vendor records, and contract renewal tracking distinct from customer-facing commercial modules.
invariants: A purchase requisition cannot become an approved purchase order without a recorded approval matching authority thresholds.
Vendor records maintain a single canonical status (active/suspended/terminated) referenced by all procurement activity.
Contract renewal reminders are computed from the contract's actual stored expiry date, never a manually re-entered date.
security: Purchase approval authority follows the same authority model as other high-impact actions.
tests: Approval-threshold enforcement is contract-tested (a requisition above a role's authority cannot self-approve).
operations: Pending approval backlog and upcoming contract renewals are observable/alertable.
recovery: Procurement and vendor records are included in backup scope.

sales.purpose: Track sales opportunities, pipeline stages, and forecasting, distinct from marketing leads and from external CRM integrations.
invariants: An opportunity has exactly one pipeline stage at a time with a full auditable transition history.
Forecast figures are always reproducible from current pipeline state, never a manually-edited number.
Sales performance metrics attribute to the actual owning rep, not whoever last touched the record.
security: Pipeline/opportunity data visibility follows role and territory assignment, not blanket access.
tests: Pipeline stage transition rules are contract-tested.
Forecast calculation is tested against known pipeline snapshots.
operations: Pipeline health (stage aging, conversion rate) is observable.
recovery: Opportunity and interaction history is included in backup scope and restore-tested.

social.purpose: Schedule, publish, and monitor content across external social media platforms, and centralize engagement replies.
invariants: A scheduled post's target platform and credentials are validated before the scheduled send time, not only at creation.
Social engagement replies are attributable to the responding staff member.
Social analytics figures are reproducible from stored platform API responses, not recomputed estimates presented as fact.
security: Social platform credentials/tokens sit behind an owned adapter boundary per platform, never hardcoded per integration.
tests: Scheduled-post failure (expired token, platform API error) has a tested retry/alert path.
operations: Post delivery failures and engagement volume are observable.
recovery: A failed scheduled post is retried or surfaced as a failure, never silently dropped.

marketplace_ops.purpose: Manage selling the same catalog across multiple third-party online marketplaces as one coordinated operation, distinct from the single-storefront Commerce/domain capabilities.
invariants: A SKU's inventory and price on any connected marketplace is always derived from the canonical product/inventory record, never edited independently per marketplace.
Automated repricing never sets a price below the merchant's configured minimum margin floor.
Marketplace settlement reconciliation flags any payout that does not match expected revenue minus fees/refunds/penalties; it never silently accepts a mismatch.

When CAP-CHANNEL-MAPPING is also selected, a marketplace-specific category/attribute mapping is derived from the canonical product/attribute record (CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES); it never becomes a second, independently-edited copy of the product's own attributes.

When CAP-LISTING-ISSUES is also selected, a listing rejection is always traced to the specific field or rule the marketplace's own response names, never reported as an opaque unattributed failure -- the same traceability CAP-PRODUCT-FEED's own feed-rejection invariant already requires for shopping/ad channels.

When CAP-MARKETPLACE-MESSAGING is also selected, a marketplace buyer message and its reply remain that marketplace's own conversation record; it is never merged into or duplicated as an internal ticket/live-chat conversation without an explicit, separate linkage.
security: Marketplace API credentials are scoped per connected account and revocable independently of other connectors.
When CAP-CHANNEL-MAPPING is also selected, authoring a category/attribute mapping rule requires the same marketplace-operations authority as other per-marketplace configuration.
When CAP-LISTING-ISSUES is also selected, per-marketplace rejection detail is only visible to authorized marketplace-operations staff.

When CAP-MARKETPLACE-MESSAGING is also selected, per-marketplace messaging credentials are scoped and revocable independently of other connected marketplace accounts, the same as this module's other marketplace API credentials.
tests: Repricing logic is contract-tested against the minimum-margin floor with an adversarial case at the floor boundary.
Settlement reconciliation is contract-tested with an intentionally mismatched payout fixture that must be flagged, not silently reconciled.

When CAP-CHANNEL-MAPPING is also selected, mapping resolution is contract-tested for a product missing a marketplace-required attribute, which must be flagged rather than published with a blank value.
When CAP-LISTING-ISSUES is also selected, rejection-reason traceability is contract-tested with a fixture rejection response that must resolve to a real, named product field.
When CAP-MARKETPLACE-MESSAGING is also selected, a marketplace's own response-time policy deadline is contract-tested for the alerting path when it is about to be missed.
operations: Per-marketplace account health (rate limits, policy warnings, sync failures) is observable and alertable.
When CAP-CHANNEL-MAPPING is also selected, unmapped or partially-mapped categories/attributes per connected marketplace are observable.
When CAP-LISTING-ISSUES is also selected, rejected-listing volume per marketplace and per rejection reason is observable and alertable.
When CAP-MARKETPLACE-MESSAGING is also selected, per-marketplace message response-time compliance is observable and alertable.
recovery: A marketplace connector outage does not block order intake from other channels; queued listing/price updates retry once the connector recovers.
When CAP-CHANNEL-MAPPING is also selected, mapping rule configuration is included in backup scope.
When CAP-LISTING-ISSUES is also selected, listing rejection/resolution history is included in backup scope.
When CAP-MARKETPLACE-MESSAGING is also selected, marketplace buyer message history is included in backup scope.

b2b.purpose: Support business (company-to-company) buyers whose purchasing process differs structurally from individual consumer checkout.
invariants: A company account's negotiated pricing and credit terms apply consistently to every buyer acting under that company, never per-individual-buyer overrides that bypass the company agreement.
An order placed against a credit-terms account cannot exceed the account's approved credit limit without an explicit override recorded with who approved it.
A quote/RFQ becomes a binding order only through an explicit conversion step, never implicitly from viewing or discussing it.
security: Company buyer roles restrict which company employees can submit vs. approve purchases, independent of the merchant's own staff roles.
tests: Credit-limit enforcement is contract-tested at and just above the limit boundary.
operations: Outstanding credit-terms balances approaching their due date are observable for collections follow-up.
recovery: Company account records, negotiated pricing, and credit terms are included in backup scope.

subscription_commerce.purpose: Sell recurring subscription products/services to end customers -- distinct from CAP-SUBSCRIPTION, which is how this generated system itself charges its own operator customers.
invariants: A subscription's next billing date and product/plan are always derived from its own recorded lifecycle state, never recomputed ad hoc from unrelated order history.
A failed recurring payment triggers the dunning process before the subscription is cancelled; it is never silently cancelled on the first failure.
A pause, plan change, or cancellation takes effect on a recorded effective date, never applied retroactively to already-fulfilled cycles.
When CAP-SUBC-CHURN is also selected, a computed churn rate is always reproducible from the subscription lifecycle's own recorded cancellation/non-renewal events, never a manually-edited number.
security: Stored payment methods used for recurring billing follow the same PCI-scope boundary as one-time payments (DER-PAYMENT-ADAPTER); no local plaintext storage.

When CAP-SUBC-CHURN is also selected, at-risk-subscriber signals are only visible to authorized staff, never surfaced to the subscriber themselves in a way that could reveal internal retention scoring.
tests: Dunning/retry logic is contract-tested across the full failed-payment-to-cancellation sequence.
When CAP-SUBC-CHURN is also selected, churn-rate calculation is contract-tested against a known lifecycle-event fixture with a hand-verified expected rate.
operations: Upcoming renewals, failed-payment recovery rate, and churn are observable.
When CAP-SUBC-CHURN is also selected, churn rate trend and at-risk subscriber count are observable, extending this module's own upcoming-renewal/failed-payment-recovery observability.
recovery: Subscription lifecycle state and billing history are included in backup scope.
When CAP-SUBC-CHURN is also selected, churn analytics history is included in backup scope.

loyalty.purpose: Reward repeat customers with points, tiers, referrals, or stored value, independent of CAP-PROMOTIONS' one-off discounts and coupons.
invariants: A customer's points balance and store-credit balance are each a single canonical ledger; no code path adjusts the displayed balance without writing a corresponding ledger entry.
Referral rewards are only granted once the referred customer completes the qualifying action (e.g. first purchase), never at signup alone, to prevent trivial abuse.
security: Gift card and store credit redemption is rate-limited/monitored to detect brute-force code guessing.
tests: Points/store-credit ledger arithmetic is contract-tested for rounding and concurrent-redemption race conditions.
operations: Unusual redemption velocity (possible fraud) is observable and alertable.
recovery: Points balances, tier status, and stored value balances are included in backup scope.

reviews.purpose: Collect and surface customer-generated product/store feedback.
invariants: A review is attributed to the customer account or contact record that submitted it; verified-purchase linkage, where the merchant wants it, is implemented via CAP-ORDERS and is not assumed by this module on its own.
Moderation state (pending/approved/rejected) is tracked per review; a rejected review never displays publicly regardless of caching.
security: Uploaded review media is scanned/validated the same as any other user-uploaded file capability, not exempted.
tests: Moderation-gating is contract-tested: a pending review must not appear in any public read path.
operations: Review volume and average rating trend are observable.
recovery: Review content and moderation history are included in backup scope.

cross_border.purpose: Handle customs, duties, and cross-border product compliance data distinct from domestic tax handling.
invariants: A product's HS code and country of origin are stored as canonical product master data, never re-entered per shipment.
Landed cost (duties/import tax) shown to a customer is computed from the actual applicable rate for the destination country, never a flat estimate presented as final.
security: Customs/compliance documents (commercial invoices, certificates) are access-controlled the same as other regulated business records, since they carry sensitive shipment and pricing data.
tests: Landed cost calculation is contract-tested across at least one de-minimis-threshold boundary case.
operations: Shipments missing required customs documentation before dispatch are observable and blockable.
recovery: HS code and compliance registry data are included in backup scope.

oms.purpose: Orchestrate order fulfillment logistics (splitting, backordering, preordering, dropshipping) beyond simple single-shipment order records.
invariants: A split order's child shipments always sum back to the original order's line items and quantities; nothing is lost or duplicated across the split.
A backordered or preordered line item is never marked fulfilled until the actual stock movement confirming it exists.

When CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is also selected, a split order's per-warehouse child shipments each source from that module's own partitioned location balance, never from an unpartitioned company-wide figure; when CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is not selected, 'different warehouses' in a split is a descriptive fulfillment-routing label only, with no location-partitioned stock record behind it.

When CAP-SHIPPING is also selected, a split order's child shipments are records in that module's own shipment/tracking system, not a second, parallel shipment concept local to this module; when CAP-SHIPPING is not selected, a 'shipment' here is a fulfillment-routing label only, with no tracking-number/carrier record behind it.

When CAP-ORDER-MERGE is also selected, a merged shipment's line items always sum back to every original order it was merged from; nothing is lost or duplicated across the merge, the same conservation invariant this module's own order-split reconciliation already requires in reverse.
When CAP-FULFILLMENT-ROUTING is also selected, a routing decision is always traceable to the specific rule that produced it, never an opaque unexplained assignment.

When CAP-ORDER-EXCEPTION is also selected, an order-fulfillment problem always produces an explicit exception record with a defined resolution state; an order is never left silently stalled with no trackable record of why.
security: Order-routing decisions (which warehouse/supplier fulfills a split) never leak cross-tenant inventory visibility in a multi-tenant deployment.

When CAP-ORDER-MERGE is also selected, merging orders across two different customers is rejected; only orders belonging to the same customer or destined for the same fulfillment location may be merged.

When CAP-FULFILLMENT-ROUTING is also selected, manually rerouting an order's assigned fulfillment source requires the same authority as other order-routing decisions; it is never available to an unauthenticated or customer-facing actor.
When CAP-ORDER-EXCEPTION is also selected, resolving an exception record requires the same order-management authority as other order-routing decisions.
tests: Order-split reconciliation (children sum to parent) is contract-tested.
When CAP-ORDER-MERGE is also selected, merge reconciliation (a merged shipment sums back to every original order) is contract-tested, mirroring this module's existing order-split reconciliation test.

When CAP-FULFILLMENT-ROUTING is also selected, routing-rule resolution is contract-tested against a fixture where the originally preferred source is unavailable, confirming fallback to the next rule-defined source.
When CAP-ORDER-EXCEPTION is also selected, exception creation is contract-tested for each of its triggering failure types (allocation failure, source rejection, address/inventory mismatch).
operations: Aging backorders and preorders past their expected date are observable.
When CAP-ORDER-MERGE is also selected, orders eligible for merge but still pending are observable.
When CAP-FULFILLMENT-ROUTING is also selected, orders that fail to resolve to any available fulfillment source are observable and alertable.
When CAP-ORDER-EXCEPTION is also selected, open exception record count and age are observable and alertable.
recovery: Order orchestration state (split/backorder/preorder/dropship routing) is included in backup scope.
When CAP-ORDER-MERGE is also selected, order-merge linkage records are included in backup scope.
When CAP-FULFILLMENT-ROUTING is also selected, routing rule configuration and routing-decision history are included in backup scope.
When CAP-ORDER-EXCEPTION is also selected, exception records are included in backup scope.

demand_planning.purpose: Forecast future demand and recommend restocking, distinct from simply recording current inventory levels.
invariants: A restock recommendation is always traceable to the forecast and safety-stock parameters that produced it, never an opaque unexplained number.

When CAP-INVENTORY-OVERSTOCK is also selected, an overstock flag is always traceable to the specific forecast and threshold parameters that produced it, the same traceability this module's own restock-recommendation invariant already requires.

When CAP-INVENTORY-AGING is also selected, a stock unit/batch's age is computed from its actual recorded receipt movement (CAP-INVENTORY's own immutable movement ledger), never a separately-maintained or manually-entered receipt date.
security: Historical demand data used for forecasting is scoped per tenant/brand in a multi-tenant deployment, never pooled across unrelated tenants without explicit consent.
When CAP-INVENTORY-OVERSTOCK is also selected, overstock signals and any suggested markdown/reallocation action are visible only to authorized inventory/merchandising staff, not customer-facing.
When CAP-INVENTORY-AGING is also selected, aging reports are visible only to authorized inventory/merchandising staff.
tests: Reorder-point calculation is contract-tested against known forecast/lead-time/safety-stock inputs with a hand-verified expected output.
When CAP-INVENTORY-OVERSTOCK is also selected, overstock threshold detection is contract-tested against known forecast/stock-level inputs with a hand-verified expected flag.
When CAP-INVENTORY-AGING is also selected, age-band classification is contract-tested against a known receipt-date fixture spanning multiple age bands.
operations: Forecast accuracy (predicted vs. actual) is tracked over time so drift can be caught.
When CAP-INVENTORY-OVERSTOCK is also selected, flagged overstock volume/value is observable over time.
When CAP-INVENTORY-AGING is also selected, stock aging into the oldest band is observable and alertable.
recovery: Forecast models and historical demand data used to produce them are included in backup scope.
When CAP-INVENTORY-OVERSTOCK is also selected, overstock detection history is included in backup scope.
When CAP-INVENTORY-AGING is also selected, aging history is derivable from CAP-INVENTORY's own backed-up movement ledger, requiring no separate backup scope of its own.

affiliate.purpose: Manage third-party promoters (influencers, affiliates) who drive sales in exchange for commission, distinct from the merchant's own marketing campaigns.
invariants: A commission is only calculated and payable against an attributed, completed, non-refunded sale -- never against clicks/views alone.
Attribution follows a single documented rule (e.g. last-click within a window) applied consistently, not an ad hoc per-case decision.

When CAP-CREATOR-SEEDING is also selected, a seeded (gifted) product unit is recorded against the creator's own record and never conflated with a commission-bearing affiliate sale in performance reporting.

When CAP-UGC-LICENSING is also selected, the merchant reusing a creator's content in its own marketing is only permitted within the scope, duration, and channels an actually-recorded usage-rights grant covers; reuse outside a recorded grant, or after it expires, is never silently allowed.
security: Promo/referral codes are rate-limited against brute-force enumeration.
When CAP-CREATOR-SEEDING is also selected, authorizing a seeding shipment requires the same partner-management authority as other creator/affiliate record changes.
When CAP-UGC-LICENSING is also selected, recording or amending a usage-rights grant requires the same partner-management authority as other creator/affiliate record changes.
tests: Commission calculation is contract-tested including a refunded-sale case that must reverse the commission.
When CAP-CREATOR-SEEDING is also selected, seeding records are contract-tested to confirm they never contribute to commission calculation.
When CAP-UGC-LICENSING is also selected, reuse-permission enforcement is contract-tested against an expired or out-of-scope grant, which must be rejected.
operations: Pending commission payouts and top-performing partners are observable.
When CAP-CREATOR-SEEDING is also selected, seeding spend (units/value gifted) per creator is observable.
When CAP-UGC-LICENSING is also selected, content whose usage-rights grant is expiring soon is observable before the merchant loses permission to keep using it.
recovery: Partner records, attribution data, and commission history are included in backup scope.
When CAP-CREATOR-SEEDING is also selected, seeding records are included in backup scope.
When CAP-UGC-LICENSING is also selected, usage-rights grant records are included in backup scope.

pos.purpose: Support physical retail point-of-sale operations distinct from purely online commerce.
invariants: In-store inventory and online inventory are reconciled against a single canonical stock record; a sale in either channel decrements the same source of truth.
A click-and-collect or ship-from-store order is not marked ready/fulfilled until the specific store location confirms the physical action.

When CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is also selected, a click-and-collect or ship-from-store order sources its stock from that specific store's own partitioned location balance -- this module's store-location fulfillment check composes with, and never duplicates, that module's per-location allocation; when CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is not selected, 'the specific store location' is a fulfillment-routing distinction only, with no location-partitioned stock record behind it.

When CAP-SHIPPING is also selected, a ship-from-store order's shipment is a record in that module's own shipment/tracking system, not a second, parallel shipment concept local to this module; when CAP-SHIPPING is not selected, 'ship the order to them' is a fulfillment-routing description only, with no tracking-number/carrier record behind it.

When CAP-POS-RECEIPT is also selected, a receipt's itemized total always reconciles to the POS transaction record it was generated from; it is never independently recalculated as a separate, potentially-diverging figure.
security: Store-level staff access to POS transaction history follows the same role-based access as other customer_service/commerce data; no separate unmanaged cash-handling data model is introduced by this module.
When CAP-POS-RECEIPT is also selected, an emailed receipt is sent only to the customer identity linked to that transaction, never an address supplied without verification at the register.
tests: Cross-channel inventory decrement (online sale reducing in-store availability and vice versa) is contract-tested.
When CAP-POS-RECEIPT is also selected, receipt generation is contract-tested for a transaction including tax and a partial/split payment method.
operations: Per-store daily reconciliation discrepancies are observable.
When CAP-POS-RECEIPT is also selected, receipt print/send failures at the register are observable.
recovery: POS transaction records are included in backup scope.
When CAP-POS-RECEIPT is also selected, issued receipts are included in backup scope and can be reprinted/resent from the original transaction record.

returns.purpose: Track the customer-initiated post-purchase return/exchange workflow (request, approval, return shipment, receiving inspection, refund-or-exchange handoff) for a product with no defect, distinct from CAP-WARRANTY, which only applies within a defect/warranty window, and from CAP-REFUNDS, which only executes the money movement, not the request/approval/inspection workflow around it.
invariants: A refund or exchange is never executed (via CAP-REFUNDS / inventory restock) before the return request has been approved.
Inventory disposition (restock, quarantine, or dispose) is only recorded after the returned item has actually been received and inspected, never on request or approval alone.
A return request always references a real, already-placed order and product; it cannot be created against an order that does not exist.

When CAP-SHIPPING is also selected, the return-shipment step (the customer sending the item back) uses that module's shipment/tracking record rather than a separate return-only shipment representation; when CAP-SHIPPING is not selected, return-shipment tracking is out of this module's scope.

When CAP-QUALITY-INSPECTION is also selected, the receiving-inspection step and its result compose with that capability's own Inspection/QualityIssue records instead of a second, parallel inspection concept; when CAP-QUALITY-INSPECTION is not selected, receiving inspection is a simple internal resellable/not-resellable check with no formal defect record.

When CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is also selected, a restock disposition increases the balance of the specific location the item was actually received back into, not an unpartitioned company-wide figure; when CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is not selected, a restock is a single company-wide balance increase as it is today.
security: A return request and its inspection result are only visible to the requesting customer and authorized staff; a customer cannot view or act on another customer's RMA.
tests: The approval-before-refund invariant is contract-tested: attempting to trigger the refund/exchange handoff on an unapproved return request is rejected.
operations: Return requests stalled past an expected inspection turnaround time are observable.
recovery: Return/RMA request and inspection records are included in backup scope.

warranty.purpose: Track product warranty coverage and repair/replacement workflows for durable goods, distinct from CAP-REFUNDS, which only covers returning money, not tracking a physical repair/replacement case.
invariants: Warranty eligibility for a claim is determined from the product's actual recorded purchase/serial data, never an unverified customer-stated purchase date.
A repair's status transitions follow a single recorded state machine; a repair is never simultaneously 'completed' and 'awaiting parts'.
security: Warranty claim lookup is restricted to the claiming customer and authorized staff; looking up by serial number alone never exposes another customer's purchase data.
tests: Warranty-eligibility determination is contract-tested against an expired-warranty boundary case.
operations: Repairs stalled past an expected turnaround time are observable.
recovery: Warranty and repair-case records are included in backup scope.

cdp.purpose: Recognize that the same real customer is contacting the business through multiple different channel identities, and record their marketing consent per channel/purpose -- distinct from CAP-IDENTITY (login accounts) and CAP-INTERACTION-HISTORY (activity log for an already-known customer).
invariants: Automatic merging of two channel identities into one customer record requires a documented confidence threshold (e.g. matching verified email or phone); it is never merged on a weak/inferred signal alone without that being recorded as low-confidence.
A merge is always reversible (unmerge) and logged with who/what triggered it.
A customer's consent status for a given channel and purpose is read from the consent ledger at the moment of sending, never assumed from a stale cached flag.
security: Consent ledger entries are immutable/append-only (a withdrawal is a new entry, not an edit of history) to support compliance audits.
tests: Identity merge/unmerge is contract-tested including a low-confidence case that must NOT auto-merge.
operations: Pending identity-merge conflicts requiring human review are observable.
recovery: Identity resolution links and the full consent ledger history are included in backup scope.

promotions.purpose: Apply discounts and conditional promotion rules to a transaction at checkout, and price the same product differently per sales channel or market -- distinct from CAP-CAMPAIGNS, which only tracks a marketing campaign's own budget/schedule/performance rather than changing what a customer pays.
invariants: A promotion or price book adjusts the amount charged at checkout; it never rewrites the product's own recorded base price.

A coupon code's redemption count and remaining uses are read from a single canonical ledger at the moment of redemption, never from a stale cached count, so the same code cannot be redeemed past its intended limit under concurrent use.
Channel/market price book resolution is deterministic for a given product, channel, and market combination -- never ambiguous between two applicable price book entries with no defined precedence.

A promotion or price book is checked against the product's configured margin floor before the discounted price is allowed to apply; a rule that would price below floor is rejected rather than silently applied at a loss.

When a marketplace/channel-sync or shopping/ad-feed capability (e.g. CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC, CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE, CAP-PRODUCT-FEED) is also selected, the price book is the resolution authority for what a customer is charged; the sync/connector/feed layer only publishes the already-resolved price outward and never writes a competing price back as authoritative.
security: Coupon code redemption is rate-limited/monitored to detect brute-force code guessing.
tests: Coupon redemption-limit enforcement is contract-tested for the concurrent-redemption race condition, and price book resolution is contract-tested for the channel+market precedence case.
Margin-floor rejection is contract-tested for a promotion rule that would price below the configured floor.
operations: Unusual coupon redemption velocity (possible abuse) is observable and alertable.
recovery: Promotion, coupon redemption, and price book records are included in backup scope.

risk.purpose: Flag suspicious orders for manual review using rules (velocity, blacklist/allowlist, promo/referral/return abuse patterns) keyed to a customer identity, and separately track the card-network chargeback/dispute case lifecycle from creation through evidence submission to a won/lost outcome, resolved through the ordinary refund workflow when money is owed back -- distinct from CAP-PAYMENTS, which owns payment authorization/capture and (via the payment provider) raw card-level fraud scoring, and distinct from account-takeover/credential-compromise detection, which is a session/credential security concern, not an order-abuse rule; this module owns only the first-party order-abuse signals a PSP cannot see, not the PSP's own fraud engine and not account security.
invariants: A risk-screening rule match produces a recommendation routed to a manual review queue, never an automatic order block or account suspension; a human reviewer's decision is the enforcement point.
A chargeback/dispute case always references a real, already-captured payment and its originating order; it cannot be created against a payment or order that does not exist.

Velocity, blacklist, and allowlist rules are evaluated against the customer identity a screened order or account belongs to (via CAP-CUSTOMER-DATA), not the order in isolation, so the same abusive actor cannot reset their risk history simply by placing a new order.
A chargeback case reaching a lost or refund-owed outcome triggers the money movement through CAP-REFUNDS' normal refund workflow, never a silent balance adjustment outside it.

Raw card-level fraud scoring remains the payment provider's responsibility (e.g. Stripe Radar); this module never re-implements or overrides that score, only consumes it, alongside its own original PSP-assigned identifier, as one optional input into the manual-review queue -- the external score's provenance is retained, not collapsed into an undifferentiated internal number.
security: Manual review queue entries and chargeback case detail are only visible to authorized staff holding risk-review permission, never to the customer whose order or account is flagged.

Authoring or modifying a velocity/blacklist/allowlist rule requires a separate, higher risk-rule-management permission than merely reviewing flagged items -- a reviewer cannot silently escalate to rule-author by holding review access alone, since a rule author could otherwise allowlist their own abuse and permanently disable screening for it.
tests: The manual-review-not-auto-block invariant is contract-tested: a rule match alone, with no reviewer action, must not change order or account state.
Chargeback case creation against a nonexistent payment or order is rejected, contract-tested the same way CAP-RETURNS tests its own order-existence guard.
operations: Manual review queue depth and average time-to-resolution, and chargeback case volume/outcome rate, are observable and alertable.
recovery: Risk-screening flag, review-queue decision, and chargeback case records are included in backup scope.

shipping.purpose: Create a shipment record for an order, obtain a tracking number, and track delivery status through to completion, plus quote/compare carrier rates, offer pickup-point/convenience-store delivery, and hand off fulfillment to a 3PL that holds the merchant's own stock -- distinct from CAP-DROPSHIP, where the supplier ships its own goods and the merchant never holds the inventory at all, and distinct from carrier API integration itself (account credentials, label format, tracking webhook shape), which sits behind DER-CARRIER-ADAPTER, not owned directly by this module's domain data.
invariants: A shipment always references a real, already-placed order; it cannot be created against an order that does not exist.
Shipping rate quoting reads a product's weight and dimensions from CAP-PRODUCTS' own catalog data, never a hardcoded or stale default value.

Per-carrier account credentials, service codes, and label/tracking payload shapes are only ever accessed through DER-CARRIER-ADAPTER; this module's own shipment/tracking domain data never embeds a specific carrier's protocol directly.

CAP-3PL requires CAP-INVENTORY because the merchant retains ownership of stock held at the 3PL's warehouse; this is never conflated with CAP-DROPSHIP, where the supplier ships its own goods and the merchant never holds that inventory. When CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is also selected, the 3PL's warehouse is one of the locations that module partitions stock across, never a stock record kept outside that partition; when CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK is not selected, the 3PL's warehouse is simply the one place this merchant's stock is held, with no location-partitioned balance to compose with.

Pickup-point/convenience-store delivery still creates and tracks a shipment through the same shipment record as any other delivery destination; it is never a parallel or duplicate shipment representation.

Shipping rate quoting only computes what a carrier would charge to move a package; it never decides what the customer is charged for shipping, discounted, or waived above a threshold -- that pricing decision belongs to the checkout/pricing layer.

When this module is also selected, every other capability whose own description or obligations mentions a shipment (CAP-RETURNS' return-shipment step, CAP-ORDER-SPLIT's per-warehouse shipments, CAP-CLICK-COLLECT's ship-to-customer path) refers to this module's shipment record, never a second parallel shipment representation of its own.
security: Shipment and tracking detail is only visible to the customer who placed the order and to authorized staff, never to another customer.

Manually overriding a shipment's carrier-reported status (`shipment.override`) requires a separate, higher permission than creating or cancelling a shipment; ordinary staff can create or cancel a shipment without being able to silently rewrite its carrier-reported delivery status.
tests: The order-existence guard is contract-tested: shipment creation against a nonexistent order is rejected, the same pattern CAP-RETURNS and CAP-CHARGEBACK use for their own existence guards.
CAP-3PL vs. CAP-DROPSHIP non-overlap is contract-tested: activating CAP-DROPSHIP alone never resolves CAP-3PL, and activating CAP-3PL alone never resolves CAP-DROPSHIP.
operations: Delivery-exception rate and carrier-specific tracking latency are observable and alertable, so a failing carrier integration is detected before it silently degrades customer-facing tracking.
recovery: Shipment, package, and tracking-event records are included in backup scope.

plm_quality.purpose: Track a self-designed or OEM/ODM product's development lifecycle from idea through sample approval to a released specification version and its bill of materials, plus incoming/outgoing quality inspection, defect and corrective-action (CAPA) tracking, and product recall -- distinct from CAP-PRODUCTS, which only holds the resulting sellable listing, and from CAP-VENDOR-MGMT, which this module references for the supplier/manufacturer relationship but does not itself own. Inspection and recall apply to any product in the catalog, self-developed or resold, independent of whether the product-development half of this module is in use at all.
invariants: A specification version, once released (approved for production), is immutable and versioned; a later change creates a new specification version rather than silently rewriting a released one.
A sample or specification version cannot advance to the next development stage without its own defined sign-off step for that stage actually having occurred.
A bill of materials line item always references an already-created development project; it cannot exist for a product with no development project record.
A quality issue's root defect is only recorded after an inspection has actually occurred, never asserted without a corresponding inspection record.
A recall is only created from a quality issue that has already been confirmed as a defect through inspection; it can never be initiated directly from an unconfirmed report.

A recall's affected-customer list is derived from actually matching the affected product (at the product/SKU level, not batch/lot -- this catalog has no batch/lot-level tracking capability, so a recall scopes to every order of the affected product/SKU) against real orders (via CAP-ORDERS/CAP-CUSTOMER-DATA), never from an estimated or assumed customer population.

When CAP-RETURNS is also selected, a customer return's receiving-inspection step composes with this module's own Inspection/QualityIssue records instead of maintaining a second, parallel inspection concept; when CAP-RETURNS is not selected, a customer return's inspection (if any) is out of this module's scope.

When CAP-FILES is also selected, inspection evidence, defect photos, sample photos, and released specification documents are stored as that module's file records rather than a module-local attachment concept; when CAP-FILES is not selected, evidence capture is limited to this module's own structured fields (checklist results, free-text notes), with no binary attachment storage of its own.

When CAP-REVIEWS is also selected, a defect reported through a customer product review can be aggregated into the same QualityIssue record as a defect found through inspection, rather than tracked as a separate, parallel complaint category; when CAP-REVIEWS is not selected, review-sourced defect signals are out of this module's scope.

This module never asserts regulatory/compliance authority over what is or is not compliant, or over recall reporting obligations themselves (compliance authority is out of scope); it only tracks the operational workflow and, per DERIVE-COMPLIANCE-RECALL, triggers the same current-regulatory-research obligation (DER-COMPLIANCE-RESEARCH) already required for other high-stakes categories such as CAP-GOV or CAP-HEALTH-DATA. Selecting recall alone does not raise this project's overall criticality/profile classification (DERIVE-COMPLIANCE-RECALL is deliberately decoupled from the `regulated`/`profile=enterprise` question set that every other DER-COMPLIANCE-RESEARCH trigger belongs to) -- the operational recall workflow and the project's overall regulatory risk posture are tracked as two separate concerns, not conflated into one.
security: Development-project, sample, specification, and BOM detail (`plm.read`/`plm.manage`) is only visible to authorized staff, never to customers, keeping product-development data separate from the PIM listing copy the customer actually sees.

Recording an inspection finding (`quality.inspect`) and approving a specification version, sample, or quality-issue disposition for the next stage (`quality.approve`) require separate permissions; a person who can record an inspection finding cannot also approve its disposition without holding the separate approval permission.
tests: The released-spec-immutability invariant is contract-tested: attempting to modify a released specification version in place is rejected; only creating a new version succeeds.
The recall-requires-confirmed-defect invariant is contract-tested: attempting to create a recall from a quality issue with no inspection record behind it is rejected.
operations: Development projects stalled past an expected stage-turnaround time, and quality issues open past an expected CAPA resolution time, are observable.
recovery: Development project, sample, specification version, BOM, inspection, quality issue, CAPA, and recall records are included in backup scope.

merchandising.purpose: Apply merchant-authored ranking overrides (boost, bury, pin-to-top, or a curated named featured set) on top of whatever product listing surface exists -- the default category/collection listing, or the surfaces CAP-SEARCH/CAP-FILTERS provide or narrow when those are also selected -- and publish current product price/availability as a feed to an external shopping or advertising channel (e.g. Google Merchant Center, Meta Catalog) with per-field rejection triage -- distinct from CAP-AI-RECOMMEND, an algorithmic (not merchant-authored) ranking signal this module does not own, and from CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE/CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC, where the transaction itself completes on a third-party marketplace rather than the merchant's own storefront. If a project selects neither CAP-SEARCH nor CAP-FILTERS, merchandising rules are still authored and versioned against the product catalog; they simply have no runtime listing surface to apply to until one is added.
invariants: A merchandising rule (boost, bury, pin-to-top, or featured-set membership) only changes the display order or inclusion of products already returned by CAP-SEARCH, CAP-FILTERS, or the default listing; it never rewrites a product's own recorded price, description, or stock level -- those remain owned by CAP-PRODUCTS/CAP-INVENTORY/CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING.
An out-of-stock product is demoted or has its availability marked accurately using CAP-INVENTORY's real, current stock level, never a cached or assumed flag.
A merchandising rule change is versioned, never silently overwritten in place, so which rule caused a given ranking outcome at a point in time can always be reconstructed.

A feed rejection is always traced to the specific product field (price, a missing required attribute, or availability) the channel's own rejection response names, never reported as an opaque, unattributed failure.

When a marketplace/channel-sync capability (CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE/CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC) is also selected, that capability's own price/inventory sync channel is a separate, transactional third-party marketplace; this module's feed is a one-way, read-only publish to a non-transactional shopping/ad channel and never writes back to or is overridden by the marketplace-sync channel's data.

Merchandising and feed capabilities function independently of whether CAP-SEARCH or CAP-FILTERS is also selected; a merchant with only category/filter browsing, only full-text search, both, or neither can still curate ranking and publish a feed, because a merchandising rule overrides whatever listing surface exists rather than depending on a specific one.

When CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING is also selected, the feed publishes the price that capability resolved for the target channel; when it is not selected, the feed publishes the product's own catalog price. A channel-reported price mismatch is always resolved by correcting the source price record (CAP-PRODUCTS or CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING), never by writing a different, feed-local price that the source record disagrees with.

When CAP-INVENTORY-COSTING or CAP-FINANCIAL-ANALYSIS is also selected, a merchandising rule may weight ranking by product margin as one additional signal; when neither is selected, ranking rules use only catalog, inventory, and merchant-authored signals -- margin-aware ranking is never assumed available.

AI-suggested merchandising rules or feed-issue diagnoses (when an AI capability is also selected) are advisory only: a suggested rule takes effect only after a human holding `merchandising.manage` approves it, and this module's AI tooling never calls an external channel's API directly -- it only informs a rule or diagnosis that the module's own publish path executes.

Autocomplete/typeahead query suggestions are now owned by CAP-AUTOCOMPLETE (the search module, not this one) -- retrieval-time engineering behavior, never a merchant-authored ranking decision this module's own rules could override. Synonym/alias mapping (e.g. treating "sunscreen" and a brand-specific term as equivalent for ranking and retrieval) remains explicitly out of scope for this module and is not owned by any capability in this catalog yet.
security: Merchandising rule authoring (`merchandising.manage`) and shopping/ad channel feed configuration (`feed.manage`) require their own permissions, separate from read-only discovery/feed analytics (`discovery.analytics.read`); viewing performance data never implies authority to change ranking rules or feed configuration.
A merchandising rule (boost, bury, pin, or featured-set membership) can only be authored by staff holding `merchandising.manage`; a customer-facing account can never directly set one.

Shopping/ad channel API credentials (e.g. Google Merchant Center, Meta Catalog) are scoped per connected channel and revocable independently of other connectors, the same as CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE's marketplace credentials.
tests: The out-of-stock-demotion invariant is contract-tested: a zero-stock product is demoted below, or has its availability marked differently from, an otherwise-equal-ranked in-stock product.
Feed rejection traceability is contract-tested: a rejected feed item's recorded reason always names a real product field, never an opaque unattributed failure.
operations: Zero-result search/browse queries and rejected feed item volume are observable and alertable, since both signal a merchandising or catalog-data quality problem needing action.
recovery: Merchandising rule (including version history) and feed configuration/build-history records are included in backup scope.

inventory_ops.purpose: Track stock at the level of an individual physical location -- one or more of the merchant's own warehouses, retail stores, or an outsourced 3PL warehouse -- so a company-wide available quantity is always the sum of location balances, stock can move between locations through a recorded transfer or arrive via an inbound receipt, and fulfillment can be sourced from a named location. Distinct from CAP-INVENTORY, which owns the one canonical stock record itself; this module only partitions and moves that same record across physical locations, it never maintains a second, parallel stock record. Warehouse-internal execution -- bin/shelf addressing, putaway, pick/pack wave planning, barcode scanning, and lot/serial/expiry tracking -- is out of scope; this module partitions and moves quantities between named locations, not what happens physically inside one.
invariants: A company-wide available quantity is always the sum of its location balances; it is never separately maintained or allowed to drift from that sum.

Stock only moves between locations through a recorded transfer naming its source location, destination location, and quantity. A transfer's source-location decrement and destination-location increment are a single atomic movement pair -- never double-counted at both locations at once, and never lost mid-transfer if interrupted partway through.

An inbound receipt (new stock arriving at a location, e.g. from a supplier) is recorded as a movement naming only a destination location and quantity, no source -- the same immutable-movement-ledger mechanism a transfer uses, not a separate one.

When CAP-CYCLE-COUNT is also selected, a physical count's discrepancy at a specific location is recorded as an explicit, attributable adjustment movement against that location's own balance, never a silent overwrite of the company-wide aggregate.

When CAP-POS, CAP-POS-INVENTORY-SYNC, or CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC is also selected, that capability's own 'single canonical stock record' invariant and this module's per-location partition are the same underlying stock record viewed along two different axes -- sales channel and physical location -- never two competing stock records: a sales channel can be given the company-wide aggregate across all locations or a declared location subset, and either way there remains exactly one canonical stock record underneath, partitioned by location, summed for the channel view.

When CAP-3PL is also selected, the outsourced 3PL's warehouse is one of the locations this module partitions stock across, never a stock record kept outside that partition -- the merchant's own retained ownership of that stock (CAP-3PL's own stated reason for requiring CAP-INVENTORY) is expressed here as one more partitioned location, not a separate accounting.

When a capability with a fulfilling store location (CAP-POS, CAP-CLICK-COLLECT) or a per-warehouse fulfillment split (CAP-ORDER-SPLIT) is also selected, each fulfilling store or warehouse is likewise one of the locations this module partitions stock across; a click-and-collect, ship-from-store, or split-shipment order sources its stock from that specific location's own balance, never from an unpartitioned company-wide figure.

When CAP-ORDERS is also selected, an order allocation always names its source location and can never exceed that location's own available quantity -- a per-location no-oversell check, distinct from and stronger than a company-wide aggregate check alone.
security: Moving or receiving stock at a location (`inventory.transfer`) is a separate permission from recording a single-location adjustment (`inventory.adjust`); holding one does not silently grant the other.
Creating, renaming, or deactivating a location (`warehouse.manage`) requires a separate, higher permission than recording an everyday adjustment, receipt, or transfer at an existing location.
tests: The partition invariant is contract-tested: summing every location's balance for a product always equals that product's company-wide available quantity.

Transfer conservation is contract-tested, including the interrupted-mid-transfer case: a transfer's source-location decrement and destination-location increment are never observed with only one side applied.

The per-location no-oversell invariant is contract-tested (when CAP-ORDERS is also selected): an allocation request exceeding its named location's own available quantity is rejected even when the company-wide aggregate would have covered it.
operations: Per-location stock discrepancy and stalled/incomplete transfers are observable, so a transfer that decremented its source but never completed its destination increment is caught rather than silently invisible in the company-wide aggregate.
recovery: Location, per-location balance, transfer, and receipt records are included in backup scope.
